sections.h2: Land documents filed in Forsyth County
sections.html:
The registry is the county's permanent file of land title papers: deeds, deeds of trust and mortgages, satisfactions, plats, leases, notices of foreclosure and a few other filings. It also takes assumed business names, rights of way, covenant agreements, UCC filings, affidavits, powers of attorney, separation and prenuptial agreements and living wills.

Wills, divorces and estates belong to the Clerk of Court instead. An heir selling an inherited Forsyth County house files the estate papers with the clerk first, then brings the deed to the register once authority is in place.

Carry in the signed original, or route it through an approved electronic vendor, on a business day during office hours.

  • At the counter: the paper comes back to you once it is recorded.
  • By mail: send the exact fee as a business check, cashier's check or money order made out to the Forsyth County Register of Deeds, plus a stamped, self-addressed return envelope. Do not mail cash.
  • Electronic: the sender signs a submitter agreement with an authorized e-recording provider and completes a memorandum of understanding. The county lists CSC, EDL, EPN, IGS and Simplifile as vendors, and files must arrive by 4:30 p.m.

A buyer is protected only once the deed is on the registry. Until then, G.S. 47-18 leaves the transfer exposed to lien creditors and later purchasers, and the time of registration decides who ranks first. The office only records. Staff cannot draft papers or give legal advice.

The charge depends on the kind of instrument and its page count.

Real estate recording fees, Forsyth County Register of Deeds
Filing typeFee
Routine document$26 through page 15, then $4 per page
Deed of trust or mortgage$64 through page 35, then $4 per page
Plat$21 per sheet
Non-standard document$25
SatisfactionNo fee
Several instruments sent as one$10 for each, on top of recording
Certified copy$5 for page one, $2 for later pages
Plain copy$.25 a page

An added $2.00 applies per party beyond 20, counting attachments and exhibits. G.S. 161-10 sets these amounts and calls them complete and exclusive. At the counter the office takes business checks, official bank checks, money orders and credit or debit cards. Cards carry a 3 percent charge with a $1.00 floor and cannot be used by phone. Personal checks and e-checks are turned away.

The seller, called the transferor in the statute, hands over the excise tax before the deed is recorded.

The charge under G.S. 105-228.30 is one dollar per $500 block of price or value, with a partial block rounded up. The county general fund keeps one half. The state half goes each month to the Department of Revenue, and the county may retain 2 percent of it. Land lying in two counties is taxed where the larger value sits.

Annual property tax is separate. It is billed to the January 1 owner, and the county suggests clearing it at closing, so a settlement statement can show both items.

A paper that misses the standard is charged an extra $25 as a non-standard document under G.S. 161-10.

  • Letter or legal size paper, typed or printed in black on white, one side only.
  • Leave three inches blank at the top of page one, keep side margins at half an inch or more, and use type of 9 points or larger.
  • The name of the instrument placed directly beneath that blank space.
  • Ink signatures in the acknowledgment, or else a certified copy of the signed original.
  • A grantee's current mailing address on a deed, and the drafter's name on the front of a North Carolina deed of trust.

The layout rules come from G.S. 161-14. Compare your draft to this list before it travels to the courthouse, since fixing a margin costs less than the surcharge.

sections.h2: Clearing an old mortgage from the record
sections.html:
The lender or noteholder cancels a mortgage by recording a satisfaction, and the office charges nothing to record one.

A deed of trust or mortgage is a security instrument that is canceled once the debt is paid. A deed is title and is never canceled. Cancellation is the job of the owner or noteholder in the county where the instrument was recorded. Forms that can do it include a satisfaction of security instrument, a trustee's satisfaction, a notice of satisfaction, a certificate of satisfaction and an affidavit of satisfaction.

Do not assume the lender has acted. Payoff papers and satisfactions are not mailed to the borrower automatically after the loan is paid in full. Call the register of deeds to check that the loan is marked satisfied before you list the house.

Parcel maps from the tax office show lot lines, but the deed holds the legal description you should rely on. Dimensions on tax maps are calculated for tax purposes only, and the acreage on a tax record may not match the deeded or platted acreage.

To find legal lot dimensions, open the Deeds tab on the parcel's property detail page or use the register of deeds lookup. Do this before a sale when a fence, a split lot or an old boundary dispute is in play.

Besides land records, the office charges for notary work and vital records, and it waives fees for some military papers.

  • Notary public: $10, and notarial acts are $5 for each signature, except when performed with an act that already carries a fee.
  • Comparing a copy for certification: $5.
  • Recording a military discharge and getting a copy: no fee, and the Thank a Veteran photo ID is also free.
  • Certified birth or death certificate: $10; marriage license: $60.

Heirs who need a certified death certificate pay $10 for it. Call the office to confirm which of these documents can be issued the same day.

A clean filing needs four things: the signed original deed, the exact fee in an accepted form of payment, the excise tax and a return envelope if you mail it. Check the deed against the layout list above, and confirm the grantee's mailing address is on it.

If a mortgage is being paid off at closing, ask the lender or your attorney who will record the satisfaction, since it costs nothing but still has to be filed. A cash sale skips the lender, so there may be no satisfaction at all if the house was owned free and clear.

Finally, ask your closing attorney to send the deed electronically before 4:30 p.m. when timing matters. Recording time decides priority, and a deed sent late in the day waits for the next business day.

The county has 159,925 households (2020 to 2024), and 2,875 building permits were issued in 2025. Median gross rent is $1,098. A busy market means a steady flow of deeds, so allow for counter and e-filing volume.

faqs.q: How much does the Forsyth County office charge for filing a document?
faqs.a: It depends on the instrument. A routine document is $26 through page 15, then $4 per page, and a satisfaction of a deed of trust is free. G.S. 161-10 backs the county's fee sheet.

faqs.q: Will the Forsyth County office accept my personal check?
faqs.a: No. Personal checks, counter checks and e-checks are turned away. Business checks, official bank checks, money orders and credit or debit cards work.

faqs.q: What is the cutoff for an e-filed deed in Forsyth County?
faqs.a: E-filed items need to land by 4:30 p.m. on a business day. Counter and mail filings follow the regular weekday hours.

faqs.q: Who covers the excise tax on a Forsyth County sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays it to the register of deeds first. The rate is one dollar per $500 block of value, and a partial block is rounded up.

faqs.q: Can staff at the Forsyth County registry help draft my deed?
faqs.a: No. The office records papers only, and state law keeps staff from giving legal advice or showing how to draft an instrument, so see an attorney.
